{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZjw88A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDKd4Q", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 89, "title": "Implement Ap x87 FNINIT and non-waiting control/status readback", "body": "## Problem

The Ap CPU cannot initialize or inspect an x87 environment. At baseline `9b9a24f813fc601f8f3e5ac638da54c80cdcef02`, `Cpu` has no FPU state, x87 opcodes reach the unsupported-instruction diagnostic, and WAIT is a no-op. SMSW's ET bit does not establish FPU execution. See the [CPU source](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9b9a24f813fc601f8f3e5ac638da54c80cdcef02/src/cpu.rs).

Implement one bounded prerequisite: CPU-local x87 environment initialization and non-waiting control/status readback in Ap real mode. Arithmetic remains subsequent required work.

## Expected outcome

Implement these four forms using original Rust:

| Encoding | Instruction | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DB E3` | FNINIT | Initialize the x87 environment |
| `D9 /7`, memory | FNSTCW m16 | Store the current control word |
| `DD /7`, memory | FNSTSW m16 | Store the current status word |
| `DF E0` | FNSTSW AX | Store the current status word into AX |

FNINIT sets CW=`037Fh`, SW=`0000h`, TW=`FFFFh`, and clears instruction/data pointers, selectors and last opcode. It marks registers empty without requiring their physical data contents to become zero. The stores transfer current state; their memory width remains two bytes with either operand size. FNSTSW AX preserves EAX's upper half. These non-waiting forms do not perform the waiting forms' pending-exception check. See Intel's [SDM Volume 2A, FINIT/FNINIT and FSTCW/FNSTCW–FSTSW/FNSTSW entries, printed pp. 3-395–396 and 3-438–443](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/782150/253666-sdm-vol-2a.pdf).

Use the target-era real-address exception contract: either CR0.EM or CR0.TS causes restartable exception 7 for the implemented forms. A store extending outside offsets `0000h..FFFFh` causes exception 13, including SS-selected destinations. Intel486 lists this differently from the modern SDM's SS exception table; document the deliberate target choice. See the Intel-authored [Intel486 PRM, printed pp. 26-97–98, 26-132 and 26-135–136](https://manuals.plus/m/d86207aaebd9b10464f2058efc61559e6141d3b072db100e89bfe17c8187e143). LOCK causes exception 6, as specified by the SDM entries above.

Model `Machine::reset` as RESET without BIST for this environment: retain its state until FNINIT. Cold construction may use initialized metadata as an explicit deterministic emulator policy. Intel486 distinguishes FNINIT/BIST initialization from RESET without BIST, which retains FPU state: [Intel486 PRM §19.2.3, printed pp. 19-2–3](https://manuals.plus/m/d86207aaebd9b10464f2058efc61559e6141d3b072db100e89bfe17c8187e143).

Preserve integer flags and unrelated registers on successful execution. Document any deterministic treatment of the stores' architecturally undefined x87 condition bits separately from hardware guarantees.

Scope excludes arithmetic, stack data operations, FLDCW, environment save/restore, numerical exception generation, NE/IRQ routing, WAIT/FWAIT completion, protected execution and paging. Other valid but unimplemented x87 instructions must remain explicitly unsupported rather than becoming aliases or successful no-ops. Preserve VM behavior, CPUID rejection and existing fixture adaptations that bypass optional FPU detection.

## Context and reproduction

Static reproduction, not executed by this evaluator: in an Ap real-mode CPU harness, execute `DB E3 D9 3E 00 80 DD 3E 02 80 DF E0`. The current decoder stops at `DB`. After implementation, the sequence should complete with `7F 03 00 00` at physical `8000h`, given zero segments, and AX=`0000h`.

Relevant integration points are `src/cpu.rs::{decode,check_mem,step,execute}`, `src/lib.rs::Machine::reset`, and `tests/cpu386.rs`. General memory helpers currently select exception 12 for SS overruns, so these target-era x87 stores require an instruction-specific preflight. Existing SMSW tests and the original [SMSW guest](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9b9a24f813fc601f8f3e5ac638da54c80cdcef02/guest/smsw.asm) provide patterns for fixed-width stores, prefix handling, restart frames and native/browser fixture validation.

Project progress: inspection of PR #88's RTC implementation and focused test changes supports the recorded Time Set/Counter Hold improvement against the [NEC µPD4990A specification, printed pp. 6–7](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/dst/upd4990a-data-sheet). No concrete recovery requirement was identified in the inspected changes. The Coordinator reports 348 native tests and 124 production release-Wasm browser cases passing. Its default browser invocation executed zero cases because port 8000 was occupied; the successful alternate-port run reportedly preserved both URL roots, assertions and budgets. No independent review or remote CI result was supplied. These are Coordinator-reported results, not tests executed by this evaluator; see the [committed validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9b9a24f813fc601f8f3e5ac638da54c80cdcef02/docs/validation.md#issue-87-ap-rtc-time-setcounter-hold).

All 26 inventory scopes remain unchanged: cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, rtc, keyboard, mouse, fdc, ide, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, pcm86, bios, lio and integration remain partial; grcg remains implemented_unverified; paging and fpu remain unimplemented. None is verified. Successful completion of this Issue would make FPU partial only.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add original native tests in `tests/fpu.rs` and, where necessary, CPU-local unit tests. Demonstrate the minimal reproduction failing before implementation and passing afterward. Use literal specification-derived expectations, independently of implementation helpers.
- [ ] Seed nondefault environment metadata in native tests. Verify FNINIT initializes every specified field, is repeatable, and clears seeded exception status without invoking a numerical exception handler. Verify stores read nondefault current words, preserve unrelated state, and do not replace initialized pointers with their own instruction/destination addresses. Tests may seed internal state directly; guest status writers are outside scope.
- [ ] Cover independent operand/address sizes, repeated size overrides, last segment override, FS/GS, 16-bit addressing, 32-bit SIB/default SS, unaligned destinations and exact-width guards. Check successful boundary stores, rejected boundary crossings and address32 offsets above the real-mode limit. Preflight before any destination write; retain existing A20 mapping and ROM protection.
- [ ] Cover exception 7 independently for EM, TS and both, using the existing CPU-local machine-status word. Cover LOCK exception 6 for all four forms and the specified store-limit faults. Assert unchanged destinations/environment on fault, first-prefix restart addresses, complete six-byte real-mode frames, and guest repair/IRET/retry. Exercise relocated IDTR delivery as well as the default IVT. Avoid asserting undocumented simultaneous-fault precedence.
- [ ] Verify CPU-instance isolation, cold-construction policy, retained environment across `Machine::reset`, and explicit reinitialization afterward. Preserve VM unsupported behavior and Ap CPUID rejection. Add a neighboring valid, unimplemented x87 encoding check to prevent overly broad decoding.
- [ ] Add an original MIT `guest/fpu_init.asm` probe, offline fixture builder and checked provenance manifest containing source/image hashes, license, assembly command, independent expected result/guard bytes and a maximum 2,000,000-slot boot budget. Exercise all four forms, prefixes, exact stores and guest fault repair. Integrate preparation into the existing README/CI flow; acquire no proprietary ROMs or guest software.
- [ ] Boot the identical hash-pinned image natively and through the production release-Wasm browser artifact at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, cold and after reset. Require exact results/guards, PASS without FAIL, no emulator/browser errors, unchanged mounted media and the stated budget. Browser hosts may mount, step, inspect and reset; they must not inject FPU state or patch results.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs `cargo test --locked --test fpu --test cpu386 --test core`, then the repository's complete README validation: lawful fixture preparation, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check` and `npm test`. Preserve existing hardware, DOS/apps, VM, audio, storage and six-game assertions and budgets. Record exact outcomes, failures/skips and any equivalent alternate-port browser invocation.
- [ ] Update directly affected hardware/compatibility documentation and validation evidence. Explicitly retain remaining FPU work: stack/load/store operations, arithmetic/comparisons/conversions, rounding/precision, control/environment operations, numerical exceptions and WAIT/NE/IRQ behavior. Protected execution, paging and other inventory gaps remain required. Limited probes and game regressions establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
